chunks: And with this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ya'qub ibn Ja'far, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that he said:

I do not say: Verily, He is definite so I remove Him from His place, nor do I bound Him to a place that He may be confined to it. Nor do I limit Him with words that are thrust from the mouth. The Blessed and Exalted says: “Be and it is,” by His Will, and without any hesitation in desire, the Peerless, the Needless. He is not in need of an associate in His Sovereignty, nor an associate to open the doors of His Knowledge for Him.

key_terms.أحد: To bound/limit (specifically with a place or direction)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Kadhim define God's transcendence beyond physical space and direction?
ai.summary: Abu Ibrahim (AS) explains the divine attributes by negating physical limitations such as direction, place, and bodily movement, affirming instead that God's command is simply 'Be' and it is. He emphasizes God's absolute unity and self-sufficiency, noting that He requires no partner in His dominion nor anyone to reveal His knowledge.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 19. And with this chain of narration, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Ya`qub ibn Ja`far, that Abu Ibrahim al-Kadhim (AS) said:

I do not say: Verily, He is definite so I remove Him from His place, nor do I bound Him to a place that He may be confined to it. Nor do I set Him a boundary that He may move within something with support or by means of limbs. Nor do I limit Him with words that are thrust from the mouth. The Blessed and Exalted says: “Be and it is,” by His Will, and without any hesitation in desire, the Peerless, the Needless. He is not in need of an associate in His Sovereignty, nor an associate to open the doors of His Knowledge for Him.
